movement_source: row 'Underlying operating expenses to underlying operating income', column 31 Dec 24 (1H25) column -> column 31 Dec 25 (1H26) column
headline: On the bank's primary (cash/underlying) basis, the Group cost-to-income ratio — underlying operating expenses to underlying operating income — decreased 50 basis points from 45.2% in 1H25 to 44.7% in 1H26 (delta -0.5ppt). This was driven by positive jaws: operating income grew 7% (6.6%) while underlying operating expenses grew 5% (5.5%), so income growth outran expense growth and lowered the ratio. On the headline basis (operating expenses to total operating income, including restructuring and notable items), the ratio rose 70 bpts from 45.2% to 45.9%, reflecting $170m of restructuring and notable items recognised in 1H26 (vs nil in 1H25).

drivers.narrative: Operating income grew 7% (6.6%) from $14,097m to $15,021m, faster than expenses, producing positive jaws that lowered the ratio. Driven by net interest income +$761m (volume growth, broadly stable margin) and other operating income +$163m (milestone payment on CommInsure sale, Gemini IPO fair value gain, higher Markets/CommSec income).

Underlying operating expenses grew 5% (5.5%) from $6,372m to $6,720m, raising the ratio. The bank's walk shows Inflation +$275m, Investment in technology +$222m, Investment in frontline and operations +$78m, Other -$6m, Productivity -$221m. Driven by wage inflation, higher FTE, technology spend on infrastructure/resilience/AI, cloud and software licensing, partly offset by productivity.

On the underlying (cash) basis, restructuring and notable items are excluded, so they contribute nothing to the -0.5ppt movement. On the headline basis, $170m of restructuring and notable items in 1H26 (vs nil in 1H25) raised the headline ratio to +0.7ppt, explaining the gap between the two bases.

disagreements.explanation: The underlying ratio excludes restructuring and notable items ($170m in 1H26 vs nil in 1H25), so it fell 50 bpts, while the headline ratio including those items rose 70 bpts. The bank's primary basis is cash, so the underlying movement is the headline.

limitations: The bank does not provide a ppt decomposition of the cost-to-income ratio movement into income and expense contributions; it states only the 50 bpts decrease and the income/expense growth rates. The ppt split is therefore left unquantified and the residual equals the full delta.

The bank does not publish a cost-to-income ratio walk/bridge chart; it provides separate income (p25) and expense (p28) walks in $m, not in ppt of the ratio, so the ratio-level contribution of each jaws component is not disclosed.
The presentation p65 walk (2H25→1H26) is a context (sequential) comparison and was not used for driver contributions.
